weight_analysis.observation: For E5, every predefined configuration from keyword/semantic 0.25/0.75 through 1.00/0.00 produced identical rankings and metrics. Semantic-only 0.00/1.00 differed.
weight_analysis.selection_rule_application: Because the ranking metrics for all keyword-positive E5 weights were identical, no positive semantic contribution had demonstrated ranking benefit. The predefined 1.00/0.00 weight is frozen rather than forcing hybrid contribution. Under the evaluated production tie-breaking rule, E5 still breaks equal keyword scores, so this configuration is not byte-for-byte identical to the standalone keyword baseline.

rationale: E5 was the strongest and safest semantic candidate on the locked selection set: it led semantic-only NDCG@3, MAP, Precision/Recall@3, and pairwise inversion rate; produced no label-0-over-label-2 inversion, no label-0 top result, and no strong exact-alias rank drop; and was perfect on the gig-to-freelancer direction under the selected configuration. BGE was the nearest quality alternative, but E5 had fewer pairwise inversions and fewer seniority/domain hard-negative promotions. MiniLM was materially faster and smaller but had a semantic hard-negative inversion and a three-rank exact-skill loss. GTE retained a hard-negative inversion even in keyword-dominant configurations. The standalone keyword baseline remained strongest overall, while every positive-keyword E5 weight produced exactly the same rankings and no paired NDCG@3 win over keyword. Therefore the evidence does not justify forcing a positive semantic weight: the predefined 1.00 keyword / 0.00 semantic configuration is selected. E5 remains the frozen model because the evaluated ranker uses semantic score as a deterministic tie-breaker even at zero semantic weight and E5 provided the safest such ordering among candidates. Runtime cost is accepted as a tradeoff for safer pair ordering: approximately 128.2 MiB cached, 675.4 MiB peak RSS, 50.8 ms for 10 candidates, and 198.8 ms for 50 candidates on the recorded Apple-arm64 CPU environment.

rejected_alternatives.reason: Fastest ranking and smaller cache, but weaker semantic quality, one label-0-over-label-2 inversion, and one strong exact-alias candidate dropped three ranks under semantic-only scoring.

Safe from hard-negative inversions, but below E5 on semantic and keyword-dominant NDCG@3 and pairwise ordering, with more seniority/domain hard-negative promotions and no meaningful size or ranking-latency advantage.
Smallest cache, but lowest selected-configuration NDCG@3, highest semantic pairwise inversion rate, and a label-0-over-label-2 inversion that remained in keyword-dominant configurations.

All positive-keyword E5 weights produced the same rankings, with zero paired NDCG@3 wins, fifteen ties, and one loss against keyword. A positive semantic contribution therefore had no demonstrated selection-set ranking benefit.
E5 semantic-only improved two queries but lost three, had lower MAP and Precision/Recall@3 than keyword, and did not beat the keyword baseline in aggregate.

known_selection_limitations: The corpus is a controlled 16-query selection partition, not real-user traffic or a statistical superiority study.
The selected 1.00/0.00 configuration still uses E5 for deterministic tie-breaking in the evaluated implementation, so it differs slightly from the standalone keyword baseline.

The selected configuration had one NDCG@3 loss against keyword: the Java-versus-JavaScript hard-negative family placed a label-0 candidate above the label-1 candidate, while retaining both label-2 candidates above it.
Two seniority/domain label-0 candidates advanced relative to keyword under E5 tie-breaking, but neither passed a label-2 candidate.
Recorded timings and memory are specific to Python 3.13.13 on Apple arm64 CPU.
holdout_policy: The locked holdout may affect claims, limitations, and future work, but it must not change this selected model, revision, input policy, or weight.
